I read this for the first time at the end of the spring, and I still find myself thinking about and wondering what was actually going on. This is the only book I have ever read that I think about almost every single day. I love it.

But anyway I'm curious as to what others think of it, and what you believe actually happened?

I feel like his psycho mother was actually the one writing the entire thing. That Zampano was all a fairytale as well as the Navidson Record and that her son was actually the baby that died at the end.

Also, I think that house is the creepiest thing. I have nightmares, and if I were ever in a place that dark and that strange, even if it wasn't moving around all over me and growling, I would freak out.

Honestly I thought the multiple framing devices made the whole thing impossible to get into. The characters in The Navidson Record weren't terribly compelling, nor Zampano, nor the mom. I thought the sort of expressionist approach to the book was such a hassle to read that I couldn't have gotten scared even if it would have been creepy if written normally.

If someone ever published an audiobook, though, I'd give that a try.

I can definitely see how the formatting could push someone away. I thought it was really strange at first, like it was an attempt by the author to do something different just because it was weird. But after reading it, it kind of fits. You don't really know what's going on in a lot of it but you think you do. The entire thing is a scary, jumbled mess just like real life and the problems people face in reality.

I don't know if there's an audio book but i know theres an ebook that isn't all wonky on the inside. Also I sort of agree that most of the characters besides Johnny and those he interacts with are a bit dry, but reflecting upon them and their actions/thoughts is what made the book for me. And the creepiness came mostly after sitting in my dark room thinking about the book, thinking about that house. I would freak out if that were real, even if it were just a dark empty hallway that didn't move around. But i totally see how this book isn't for everyone.

If you liked that, I can recommend The Dionaea House, which is online in it's entirety. It got it's author a job as Hollywood scriptwriter, unfortunately, the movie version of Dionaea House never got made and he has since written the scripts for the Nightmare on Elm Street reboot and The Thing prequel.
